What is less obvious is how that choice looked at the time, when some analysts were leaning into a 6G and AI supercycle narrative while others saw only modest upside. The Two Nokia Stories Investors Had To Weigh

The shares cost €5.2 at the start of the period, and you had to decide which Nokia story felt more realistic.

The bullish narrative saw Nokia as a 6G and AI infrastructure winner, with a fair value of €5.75, a price implied by forecasts that revenue would grow 5.9% a year and margins would roughly double.

The more cautious view put fair value at €4.43, a price implied by slower 3.0% annual revenue growth and concerns that Mobile Networks and hyperscaler exposure might stay weaker than hoped.

What The Nokia Evidence Actually Tested

The clearest datapoint came from Nokia’s Q3 2026 figures. Revenue was €5,154m against €4,700m a year earlier and net income excluding extra items was €173m against €88m. Net margin moved from 1.9% to 3.4%. That shift nudged results toward the bullish story on earnings power, although the cautious case on execution risk and competition still mattered.

The lesson is simple. When a 6G or AI pitch is central, track whether margins and absolute profit move together in reported numbers, rather than focusing only on whether sales and headlines sound exciting.

What Nokia's Recent Run Now Prices In

Nokia trades at €6.44, which is above the Fair Value implied by the bearish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St. That view treats the recent 28.0% gain over the past year as already baking in meaningful delivery on the AI and cloud story.

The Narrative’s case leans on Nokia shifting toward higher margin AI, cloud and Network Infrastructure activities while executing a heavy restructuring load. A buyer today is effectively assuming AI related demand turns into durable profit, so how secure does that look if supply constraints or cost programs slip?

"The numbers imply the share price already reflects strong delivery on AI and cloud growth, execution on indium phosphide capacity ramps, and improved Network Infrastructure margins, leaving limited room for disappointment and pointing to Nokia Oyj as overvalued on this narrative."

Another Angle On Nokia’s Theme

Nokia points you toward networks and the plumbing behind AI buzz. Step back and a different hardware angle appears.

People still reach those networks through devices in their pockets, on their wrists and on their desks. Those everyday gadgets are becoming AI hubs themselves.

One large consumer brand is leaning into that shift. It is designing custom chips and software so AI tasks run directly on personal devices.

That move tries to weave hardware, services and payments more tightly together. If it succeeds, your next upgrade choice might center on an ecosystem, not just a phone.
